newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Unusual loss seen in Nam Pei Hong unit.
newsitem.headline: Unusual loss seen in Nam Pei Hong unit.

text.p: Nam Pei Hong (Holdings) Ltd said on Friday it had filed a report with Hong Kong police relating to a HK$58 million exceptional loss for the six months to September 30 due to an abnormal shortfall in investories.

In a statement, Nam Pei Hong said one of its major wholly owned retailing and wholesaling units had recorded turnover of HK$51 million during the six-month period, trading gross profit of HK$17 million and an exceptional loss resulting from a shortfall in inventories of HK$58 million.

"Allegations have been made to the directors which suggest that there may have been wrongdoing at the time of the stock-take carried out for the audited accounts for the year ended March 31, 1996, which may have led to a misstatement of the value of these stocks as at that date," the statement said.
"This matter has been reported to the police," it said.

The company said it had carried out investigations into the operations of the group and had appointed its auditors to look into the group's existing control systems and advise on improvements to prevent future losses.
"The group has sufficient working capital and other resources for its present purposes," it said. "The director considers it should operate as usual for the foreseeable future."
The Chinese medicine retailer also said it had delayed its interim results announcement to January 6 from December 30 due to possible rationalisation with Tung Fong Hung (Holdings) Ltd.
Trading in Nam Pei Hong shares was suspended on December 23.
